sections.title: The Believer's Union with Christ
observations: In this section, Paul emphasizes the believer's identification with Christ in His death and resurrection. This union signifies that just as Christ was raised from the dead, believers too are raised to newness of life. This transformation is not merely symbolic but a profound reality that affects the believer's daily life and conduct.
The act of baptism serves as a public declaration of this union, symbolizing the believer's death to sin and resurrection to a new life in Christ.

sections.title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
observations: Paul argues that since believers have died to sin, they should no longer live in it. This raises the question of whether grace allows for continued sin, to which Paul emphatically responds with 'By no means!'.
The concept of being alive to God is crucial; it means that believers are now empowered to live righteously, reflecting the character of Christ in their lives.

sections.title: Presenting Ourselves to God
observations: In this section, Paul instructs believers to present themselves to God as instruments of righteousness. This is an active choice that reflects the believer's new identity in Christ.
The idea of being slaves to righteousness contrasts sharply with being slaves to sin. Paul highlights that the outcome of righteousness is sanctification, leading to eternal life.

sections.title: The Consequences of Sin and Righteousness
observations: Paul concludes the chapter by contrasting the wages of sin, which is death, with the gift of God, which is eternal life through Jesus Christ. This stark contrast serves as a reminder of the serious consequences of sin and the incredible grace offered through Christ.

importantVerses.commentary: How can we who died to sin still live in it? This verse encapsulates the core of Paul's argument about the believer's relationship to sin after coming to faith in Christ.
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. This verse highlights the ultimate consequence of sin versus the grace of God.

questions: What does it mean to be dead to sin and alive to God in practical terms?
How should the truth of our union with Christ affect our daily choices and behaviors?
In what ways can we actively present ourselves as instruments of righteousness?
